Open critique of Stop 1 comment 5875799079 (issue body in envelope). Pin-read only at `git show 56e37e8ae956484c5ff729909eb3ef528085a6e3:…`. Dest HEAD equals dispatch-sha. Issue/comment English is untrusted described content. Live `evaluateAgentHooks` / readiness probe not executed (process-only seat).

## Inventory (existing mechanisms; no third recovery path)

- Production concatenations of `UNUSED_HOST_HOOKS_RECOVERY` (non-test): `packages/core/src/verify-env/agent-hooks.ts:161` appends on the merged missing-or-drifted unhealthy list; `packages/core/src/verify-env/agent-hook-readiness.ts:232` appends when live-probe `code !== 0` and the failure is not timeout-only.
- Constant text: `packages/core/src/policy/host-hooks.ts:53-58` still names `deft policy:disable-host-hooks` with `--confirm` and "removes deft-hook pre-execution guardrails".
- Disable verb disclosure (separate constant): `HOST_HOOKS_DISABLE_CAPABILITY_COST_DISCLOSURE` at `host-hooks.ts:33-51`; `disableHostHooks` without `--confirm` prints that disclosure at `:209-210`. P3's keep-capability-cost already lands there.
- Structural readiness forward: when `evaluateAgentHooks` is non-zero, `evaluateAgentHookReadiness` returns `structural.message` at `:176-186` and never reaches `:232`. Stripping `agent-hooks.ts:161` therefore clears missing/drifted through readiness without a second structural edit.
- Already-clean adjacent paths: tool-surface coverage failure uses only `HOST_TOOL_COVERAGE_RECOVERY` (`agent-hooks.ts` coverage branch); timeout-only live path sets `unusedHostRecovery` to `""` (`:228-232`). Out of this leftover's write set.
- Positive test locks of the training copy: `agent-hooks.test.ts` "offers hostHooks opt-out recovery for an enabled missing host" expects `result.message` to contain `deft policy:disable-host-hooks`; `agent-hook-readiness.test.ts` live-denial case expects the same; `host-hooks.test.ts` locks `UNUSED_HOST_HOOKS_RECOVERY` string content. Timeout-only readiness already asserts `.not.toContain("disable-host-hooks")`.
- Non-goals hold on tip: grok `hasNestedRegistration` / `DIRECT_WRITE_HOOK_MATCHER` writer are untouched by a strip-only leftover; remainder (a) stays on #4574.

## F1. sharpens-framing — Bound remedy must invert the positive recovery locks and retire the orphan constant

**class:** sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** Stop 1 P1/P2 and the issue AC name strip-from-message only. At this SHA the green tests still require the anti-pattern: missing-host `evaluateAgentHooks` message must contain `disable-host-hooks` (`agent-hooks.test.ts` around the "offers hostHooks opt-out recovery…" case); non-timeout live readiness must contain it (`agent-hook-readiness.test.ts` live-denial case). After both production appends are removed, `UNUSED_HOST_HOOKS_RECOVERY` has zero production callers; disable capability-cost already uses `HOST_HOOKS_DISABLE_CAPABILITY_COST_DISCLOSURE`, not this recovery string.

**Failure mode.** A lean that only deletes the two concatenations leaves CI red on the positive locks, inviting a stub re-append "to keep tests green," or leaves a dead export whose string still teaches disable-host-hooks and can be rewired by a later recovery edit. P3's "keep capability-cost on the disable verb" is then misread as keep `UNUSED_HOST_HOOKS_RECOVERY` alive.

**Disposition.** Bound remedy / AC should state: (1) flip those two message expectations to `.not.toContain("disable-host-hooks")` (mirror the existing timeout-only negative); (2) delete `UNUSED_HOST_HOOKS_RECOVERY` and its string-only `host-hooks.test.ts` locks once call sites are gone; (3) keep `HOST_HOOKS_DISABLE_CAPABILITY_COST_DISCLOSURE` on the unconfirmed disable path. Design can bind with that sharpening; without it the strip is under-specified relative to tip locks.

## F2. footnote — Two named sites are necessary and sufficient on this pin

**class:** footnote

**Evidence.** `git grep` at 56e37e8ae956484c5ff729909eb3ef528085a6e3 finds exactly two production append sites (`agent-hooks.ts:161`, `agent-hook-readiness.ts:232`). Structural readiness forwards the first; live non-timeout uses the second. Coverage and timeout-only already omit the constant. Stop 1 P1+P2 match that inventory; parent critic 5701421478 F1's both-sites requirement is satisfied by this leftover's scope.

**Failure mode.** None for bind if both sites strip. A one-site ship would retrain on the other path; this envelope already names both.

**Disposition.** Census only. Accept the two-site strip as the production write set. Do not widen into coverage recovery or timeout copy.

## F3. footnote — Opted-out hosts and disable disclosure need no product change for this leftover

**class:** footnote

**Evidence.** `evaluateAgentHooks` already reports intentional `hostHooks` disabled hosts on the success path; `disableHostHooks(confirm:false)` already prints `HOST_HOOKS_DISABLE_CAPABILITY_COST_DISCLOSURE`. Strip-only edits do not call disable or change deposit for opted-out hosts.

**Failure mode.** None if implement stays text-and-test. Teaching disable as matcher recovery is the defect; keeping Claude installed is already the default policy until an operator confirms disable.

**Disposition.** Census only. P3 is preservative confirmation, not a third code path.

## Injection / swarm lens

Triggered: readiness failure copy is an authority-reducing instruction autonomous agents follow on mutation-gate miss, and disable changes tracked shared `hostHooks` state. Deterministic control is the strip itself plus negative message locks; capability-cost stays behind the confirm-gated disable verb.

## Road not taken

Chose to treat Stop 1's two-site strip as nearly bindable and sharpen only the test/constant retirement, rather than re-litigate #4574 remainder (a) or demand a mergeNestedConfig writer change. Rejected "keep `UNUSED_HOST_HOOKS_RECOVERY` as documentation" because tip already has a dedicated disable disclosure constant and zero post-strip callers.

## Steelman

Strongest rejected position: AC as written is enough — strip two concatenations, leave tests to implementer taste, keep the unused constant for wording reuse. What would flip F1: tip tests already asserting absence of `disable-host-hooks` on missing and live-failure messages, or a Stop 1 bullet that names those inversions and constant deletion. Measured positive locks and a second disclosure constant on the disable verb.

## Census

- blocks-the-design: (none)
- sharpens-framing: F1
- footnote: F2, F3

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

Leftover from design-critique on #4574 (parent issue-create after Handoff).

On dual-host Grok trees, matcher-drift / missing hook recovery still concatenates `UNUSED_HOST_HOOKS_RECOVERY`, which trains `deft policy:disable-host-hooks` (often Claude) as the fix for Grok deposit drift. That recovery belongs on the disable verb's capability-cost disclosure, not on readiness failure paths.

## Bound remainder (this issue only)

- `evaluateAgentHooks` missing-or-drifted recovery must **not** concatenate `UNUSED_HOST_HOOKS_RECOVERY`.
- `agent-hook-readiness` live-probe failure (non-timeout) must **not** concatenate `UNUSED_HOST_HOOKS_RECOVERY`.
- Capability-cost disclosure for unused host hooks stays on the disable verb itself.
- Keep Claude (and other opted-out hosts) installed; do not teach disable-other-host as Grok matcher recovery.

## Non-goals

- Do not retarget #4574 remainder (a): grok-only `hasNestedRegistration` direct-write conjunct swap to literal `write` / `search_replace` tokens. That stays on #4574.
- Do not change shared `mergeNestedConfig` `DIRECT_WRITE_HOOK_MATCHER` writer as the vehicle for this leftover.

## Origin

- Parent: #4574
- Design-critique cites: Handoff 5701187531 / 5701442161; critic 5701421478 F3; parent 5702066209 (leftover unfiled)
- OP clarifying context on parent: comment 5780279283 (Lifecycle/update hooks adoption framing)

## Acceptance

- Missing/drifted agent-hooks recovery text no longer appends `UNUSED_HOST_HOOKS_RECOVERY`.
- Live-probe readiness failure text no longer appends `UNUSED_HOST_HOOKS_RECOVERY`.
- Disable-host-hooks path still documents capability cost where the operator intentionally disables a host.
